also.hook: Yang forced automation and AI's threat to jobs onto the American political stage years before generative AI made the subject unavoidable, building an entire 2020 presidential campaign, and a signature policy proposal, around the argument that AI-driven job loss required a fundamental rethink of the social safety net.
also.name: Andrew Yang
also.moniker: Politician Who Made Automation a National Issue

also.hook: Preston moved from running two federal agencies during the 2008 financial crisis to leading Goodwill Industries, where he has directed the organization's push to use AI-enabled training tools to help workers displaced by automation move into new careers, applying crisis-era public administration experience to AI's labor disruption.
also.name: Steve Preston

name: Economists and Labor
blurb: Economists and labour researchers measuring what AI does to work, wages and productivity.

profiles.hook: Brynjolfsson has spent three decades building the empirical case for how digital technology, and now AI, actually changes productivity and jobs, work that shifted from academic papers to boardroom strategy as generative AI forced every company to ask the same question he had been measuring for years.
profiles.name: Erik Brynjolfsson
profiles.moniker: Economist of the Second Machine Age
